record.paper_title: Results and open problems in matchings in regular graphs
record.original_question: For infinite cubic connected graphs with no bridges, what is the correct analog of the asymptotic lower matching conjecture for matching entropy?

evidence.quote: Second, what is the analog of the ALMC for infinite cubic connected graphs with no bridges?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. For a finite graph $G=(V,E)$, let $m_k(G)$ denote the number of matchings of size $k$ in $G$ (a matching being a set of pairwise non-adjacent edges). Define the matching entropy of $G$ at density $p \in [0,1]$ by
$$h_G(p) = \frac{1}{|V|}\log m_{\lfloor p|V|/2 \rfloor}(G).$$
The Asymptotic Lower Matching Conjecture (ALMC) asserts a sharp asymptotic lower bound on $h_{G_n}(p)$ for sequences $(G_n)$ of $d$-regular graphs with $|V(G_n)| \to \infty$: namely, for every $d$-regular graph $G$ on $n$ vertices and every $p \in [0,1]$,
$$\frac{1}{n}\log m_{\lfloor pn/2\rfloor}(G) \;\ge\; \frac{1}{2}\Big(p\log d - p\log p - 2(1-p)\log(1-p) + (d-p)\log(1-p/d)\Big) + o(1),$$
with the inequality becoming asymptotically tight on suitable sequences (e.g., disjoint unions of $K_{d,d}$).

Problem. Formulate and establish the correct analog of the Asymptotic Lower Matching Conjecture for the class of infinite cubic ($3$-regular) connected bridgeless graphs. More precisely, identify the sharp lower bound function $f(p)$ such that for every infinite cubic connected bridgeless graph $G$ (interpreted via Benjamini–Schramm limits, or through finite cubic bridgeless exhaustions), the normalized logarithm of the number of matchings of edge-density $p$ satisfies
$$\liminf_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{|V(G_n)|}\log m_{\lfloor p|V(G_n)|/2\rfloor}(G_n) \;\ge\; f(p)$$
for all $p \in [0,1]$, with $f$ being best possible across the class of cubic bridgeless graphs, and determine the extremal sequences attaining $f(p)$.
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution of an analog of the Asymptotic Lower Matching Conjecture specifically for infinite cubic bridgeless graphs was located. Related results (Schrijver-style lower bounds for bipartite regular graphs, the Lovász–Plummer conjecture proven by Esperet et al. 2011, and asymptotic counts for random cubic planar graphs by Noy et al.) exist, but the precise bridgeless-cubic ALMC analog appears to remain unresolved.

status_evidence.title: On the expected number of perfect matchings in cubic planar graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Expected number of perfect matchings in random cubic planar graphs is asymptotically cγⁿ with γ ≈ 1.14196.
status_evidence.claim: Asymptotic counts for matchings in cubic graph classes are an active area; no bridgeless ALMC analog stated.

status_evidence.title: On cubic bridgeless graphs whose edge-set cannot be covered by four perfect matchings
status_evidence.snippet: Studies on perfect matchings of cubic bridgeless graphs, related to Berge-Fulkerson conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Work on cubic bridgeless graph matchings continues; entropy ALMC analog not addressed.
